packages.title: The English widget reads “Dictate a task”, like the voice shortcut and the app
brief: UX-1657 (S1), regression R2D-1 from P222 (`.claude/ux-review/runs/2026-10-19-app/verify-b7-r2-D.md`). What round 2 did, and keep it: the widget got its own string, `capture_widget_label` (`App/android/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml:11`), and every widget surface names it (the layout's text and contentDescription, `res/layout/capture_widget.xml:6` and `:10`; `CaptureWidget.kt:25`; the `.CaptureWidget` receiver's label, `AndroidManifest.xml:58`); the English voice shortcut's long label `capture_voice` became “Dictate a new task” (`strings.xml:3`). Review D confirmed UX-1656 fixed. Why this package: in English only, the voice shortcut now says “Dictate a new task” while the widget, which does the same thing, still says “Say a task”, and the in-app English copy says “dictate” throughout (`app_en.arb:1663`, `:1674`, `:1680`, `:1688`). One idea, one name. Spanish and Catalan already use one word for both (widget and shortcut «Dictar una tarea» / «Dicta una tasca»), so only English changes. This is review D's fix; it is not a product decision. It keeps a voice wording on the widget, as today, so it leaves UX-910 (the open owner question about the widget and voice shortcut's wording at 0 dictations left) where it was: whatever the owner answers there will change `capture_widget_label` and `capture_voice` together.

1. `App/android/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml` only (English): `capture_widget_label` “Say a task” → “Dictate a task” (14 characters, under the 20 its comment allows; Spanish «Dictar una tarea», 16, already shows whole in the same cell at 2.0). `capture_widget_description` “Tap to say a task.” → “Tap to dictate a task.”. Keep `capture_widget_label`'s translator comment and its place (after `capture_text_short`, before `capture_widget_description`). Don't change any other string in the file.

2. `App/lib/l10n/app_en.arb:404`, `homeCaptureInstructions`: replace “the Say a task widget” with “the Dictate a task widget”, so it reads exactly: “On Android, long-press the TaskFlow icon for its shortcuts, or add the Dictate a task widget from your launcher. Share text to TaskFlow from another app.”. It has no `@homeCaptureInstructions` entry today: add one right after it, `"@homeCaptureInstructions": {"description": "Settings, Other: how to reach capture from outside the app. Names the home-screen widget by its label (capture_widget_label in android/app/src/main/res/values/strings.xml); keep the two the same."}`. Spanish (`app_es.arb:228`, «…el widget de micrófono…») and Catalan (`app_ca.arb:207`, «…el giny Dicta una tasca…») stay exactly as they are; they already match their widgets. Run `flutter gen-l10n`.

3. Tests this change rightly breaks, in `App/test/native_resources_test.dart`; update only the English expectations: 'UX-121: the widget picker says Toca para dictar una tarea. in EN, ES and CA' (line 163), `en['capture_widget_description']` → 'Tap to dictate a task.'; the UX-1656 test whose name ends 'the widget’s label, TalkBack name and picker name are unchanged' (from line 815): its `en['capture_widget_description']` (line 825) → 'Tap to dictate a task.' and its loop's English expectation (line 857) → 'Dictate a task' (keep the ES and CA expectations and the four-surface lookup; rename the test so it no longer says the English widget is unchanged, for example '…the Spanish and Catalan shortcut labels and widget are unchanged; the English widget reads Dictate a task on every surface'); 'UX-1656: capture_widget_label reads Say a task / …' (line 884): `en['capture_widget_label']` → 'Dictate a task', and its name to match. Search the rest of `App/test/` for “Say a task” and “say a task” and update any other English expectation of these three strings the same way. Run the whole suite and build the debug APK (`flutter build apk --debug --no-pub --target-platform android-x64`) so the resources link.

Don't touch: `capture_voice`, `capture_voice_short`, `capture_text`, `capture_text_short` in any language; every `values-es` and `values-ca` string; `res/layout/capture_widget.xml`, `CaptureWidget.kt`, `CaptureShortcuts.kt`, `AndroidManifest.xml`, `res/xml/capture_widget_info.xml`; the share toasts; any ARB key other than `homeCaptureInstructions` (and its new `@` entry), and the Spanish and Catalan ARB files; P195's icon resources; the other session's files (Backend/, App/pubspec.yaml, App/scripts/, App/config/); git state.
acceptance: `res/values/strings.xml`: `capture_widget_label` is “Dictate a task” (at most 20 characters), still preceded by its translator comment and placed after `capture_text_short` and before `capture_widget_description`; `capture_widget_description` is “Tap to dictate a task.”.

In English, the voice entries share one word: `capture_voice` “Dictate a new task”, `capture_voice_short` “Dictate” and `capture_widget_label` “Dictate a task” all start with “Dictate”; no English Android string contains “Say a task” or “say a task”.

Every widget surface (the layout's text and contentDescription, the `getString` in `CaptureWidget.kt`, the `.CaptureWidget` receiver's label) names `capture_widget_label`, which reads “Dictate a task” / «Dictar una tarea» / «Dicta una tasca» in EN / ES / CA.

Settings, Other, in English: `homeCaptureInstructions` reads “On Android, long-press the TaskFlow icon for its shortcuts, or add the Dictate a task widget from your launcher. Share text to TaskFlow from another app.”, and the widget name it contains equals `capture_widget_label` in `res/values/strings.xml`; `app_en.arb` has an `@homeCaptureInstructions` description.

In Spanish and Catalan nothing changed: every `values-es` and `values-ca` string, and `homeCaptureInstructions` in `app_es.arb` and `app_ca.arb`, read as before; the English shortcut strings `capture_voice`, `capture_voice_short`, `capture_text`, `capture_text_short` read as before.
`native_resources_test.dart`: the UX-121 and UX-1656 tests expect the new English values and keep their Spanish and Catalan expectations; the whole suite passes and the debug APK links.
deviceChecks: Emulator lane, TaskFlow in English at Android's 2.0 and at 1.0: the home-screen widget's label reads «Dictate a task» whole, on at most two lines, not cut; TalkBack names it «Dictate a task»; the widget picker lists it as «Dictate a task» with «Tap to dictate a task.» under it.
Emulator lane, Android 13+: with the phone in Spanish and TaskFlow's language set to English, an already placed widget reads «Dictate a task» after the app opens (the `CaptureWidget.kt` path).
Emulator lane, Spanish and Catalan at 2.0: the widget still reads «Dictar una tarea» / «Dicta una tasca», whole (no change expected).
